newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes slip after hurricane threat disappears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes slip after hurricane threat disappears.

text.p: U.S. crude prices slipped Monday morning after the threat of hurricane damage to Gulf Coast facilities disappeared over the weekend.

Reports Iraq formally submitted an aid distribution plan to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan added to sentiment for weaker prices, with losses aimed at testing August NYMEX futures support around the $19.00 a barrel barometer.
Annan was expected to approve the aid plan by the end of July, setting the stage for resumed Iraqi exports from early August, traders said.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 5-10 cents lower at $19.15-25 a barrel.

Cash grade prices were mostly steady, with a bearish twinge. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at 20-23 cents over the August marker, and West Texas Sour/Midland was dealt at $1.22 and $1.25 under WTI/Cushing.

Sour barrels have been in retreat since late last week, following the resumption of Cano Limon production in Colombia. Even though Ecopetrol said force majeure remained in place on Covenas exports, the WTS market failed to adjust.
Colombian rebels forced the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline to shut from July 6 after repeated bombings.
Other deals were seen for WTI/Cushing Postings Plus at $1.74, $1.78 and out to $1.85. August/September WTI spreads were -22 cents, marking a depression in front month values.
